picks.title: NextEra to Buy Dominion for $67 Billion to Form Power Giant
picks.summary: This is the biggest power acquisition ever, creating a utility colossus stretching from Florida to Virginia's data centers. The deal directly addresses the massive power demands from AI infrastructure buildout, making it a pure play on the most important secular trend in markets right now.

picks.title: Global bond rout deepens as Iran war drags on and underscores inflation fears - Reuters
picks.summary: Bond yields hitting multi-year highs across the globe signals serious inflation concerns from the Iran conflict. When the long bond gets crushed like this, it ripples through every asset class — mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs, equity valuations all get repriced.

picks.title: Iran war saddles global companies with $25 billion bill - and counting - Reuters
picks.summary: A $25 billion hit to corporate bottom lines from the Iran war is real money that flows straight to earnings estimates. This kind of supply chain disruption cost gets baked into forward guidance and margin compression across multiple sectors — energy, shipping, manufacturing.

contrarian.headline: But: Bond markets signal utility mega-deals face financing headwinds
contrarian.argument: While NextEra's $67 billion Dominion acquisition creates a utility giant positioned for AI power demand, bond traders are pricing in much higher interest rates that could severely constrain financing for such massive deals. The ominous bond trades pointing to elevated borrowing costs may force utilities to scale back expansion plans just as power demand surges, creating a supply-demand mismatch that benefits smaller, nimbler players over debt-heavy consolidators.

picks.title: Global bond rout deepens as prolonged Iran war heightens inflation risk - Reuters
picks.summary: This is the big kahuna — a global bond selloff driven by Iran war inflation fears hits every asset class and central bank policy worldwide. When the long bond gets whacked this hard, it's not just about oil prices anymore; it's about whether central banks can keep the inflation genie in the bottle while funding costs spike across the board.

picks.title: NextEra to Buy Dominion for $67 Billion to Form Power Giant
picks.summary: A $67 billion utility mega-merger creates the biggest power company in America, stretching from Florida to Virginia's data center alley. This isn't just about rate base expansion — it's about who controls the electricity feeding the AI boom, and it'll ripple through every utility stock and renewable energy play on the tape.

picks.title: Brent oil tops $110 on report U.S. views latest Iranian proposal as insufficient
picks.summary: Oil punching through $110 on failed Iran peace talks means the Strait of Hormuz stays shut and energy costs keep climbing. This feeds directly into the bond rout story — higher oil means stickier inflation, which means central banks stay hawkish longer, which means everything from airlines to truckers gets squeezed harder.

contrarian.headline: But: Bond selloff may signal overheated AI infrastructure spending
contrarian.argument: While markets focus on Iran war inflation risks, the bond rout could actually reflect concerns about unsustainable AI infrastructure investments driving up long-term rates. If AI companies are borrowing heavily to fund data centers and chip purchases, this creates structural demand for credit that has nothing to do with geopolitical oil shocks—suggesting the selloff may persist even if Middle East tensions ease.

picks.title: US 30-Year Yield Hits Highest Since 2007 on Inflation Angst
picks.summary: The long bond hitting levels not seen since before the financial crisis is a massive red flag for every asset class. When the 30-year Treasury yield spikes like this, it's telling you the bond vigilantes are back and they're worried about sticky inflation from the Iran war. This moves everything - mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs, equity valuations - the whole tape gets repriced when Uncle Sam has to pay 5%+ on the long end.

picks.title: Trump says holding off on Iran attack planned for Tuesday
picks.summary: When the President calls off a military strike at the last minute, oil traders and defense contractors feel it immediately. This kind of geopolitical whiplash moves crude, the dollar, and safe-haven flows in real time. Markets hate uncertainty, but they hate the threat of supply disruption in the Strait of Hormuz even more - this pause gives everyone a chance to breathe.

picks.title: Meta layoffs starting this week stress harsh AI reality inside Zuckerberg's company
picks.summary: When Meta cuts 8,000 jobs while everyone's drunk on AI euphoria, it's a reality check for the whole sector. This isn't just about one company - it's about the brutal math of AI transformation hitting even the biggest players. If Zuck is slashing headcount to fund his AI pivot, every tech CEO is watching and taking notes.

contrarian.headline: But: AI earnings optimism could override bond market fears
contrarian.argument: While 30-year yields are spiking, the AI earnings cycle may be powerful enough to sustain equity valuations despite higher discount rates. With Nvidia earnings approaching and the broader AI infrastructure buildout still in early innings, growth expectations could trump bond vigilante concerns in the near term.
